Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

critic noun

one who finds fault with a person or a plan

also critics, his critics, detractor, fault-finder

classical

Cic. Ac. 2.7: restat ūnum genus reprehēnsōrum
Cic. Planc. 8: reprehēnsor comitiōrum (Lewis & Short)

reprehēnsor, reprehēnsōris m.

noun, third declension

a critic, one who finds fault

From reprehendere, to find fault with: the critic of a person, a decision or a book.

Other words

  • obtrectātor, obtrectātōris m. — a detractor, disparager

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 1.31: obtrectātōrēs autem et invidī Scīpiōnis; Cic. Brut. 2: laudum meārum (Lewis & Short)

    Stronger than reprehēnsor: one who runs another down, often from envy or rivalry, as its pairing with invidī shows.

Examples

  • Restat ūnum genus reprehēnsōrum, quibus Acadēmīae ratiō nōn probātur.

    There remains one kind of critic: those who do not approve of the Academy’s method.Cic. Ac. 2.7

See also criticism, critic, attack.

SourcesLewis & Short: reprehensor · Lewis & Short: obtrectator
